John Sauer is counsel of record for federal agencies and the President of the United States.

The authoritative context freezes sal-v7 band baseline and cert_anchor.rate 0.051512996760685784, although the petitioners are the National Park Service and other federal parties represented by the Solicitor General. This appears inconsistent with the prompt's federal caption-class arrival guidance and may affect the scoring benchmark. I preserve the supplied conditioning unchanged, acknowledge its 652/12657 strictly-prior baseline pool, and separately use the published federal arrival comparison of 155/212 (73.11%) over Terms 2017-2025. The high forecast rests principally on the provisioned August 31 stay opinion, not on reclassifying the harness's band. Please review the caption classification.

context.json froze band 'baseline' (cert_anchor 0.0515, the private-class floor), but the caption is a federal petitioner (National Park Service et al., President Trump; SG D. John Sauer counsel of record). The caption-class rule should read 'federal' (pooled reached rate about 73%). The forecast anchors on the federal floor; scoring against 0.05 will misstate skill.

In record/snapshots/2026-11-07.json, RelatedCaseNumber[0] has DisplayCaseNumber='26-199, 26-201, 26-332, 26-335' and RelatedType='Vide', but context.json has vide_links=[] and no record/related/ snapshots were provisioned, likely because DisplayCaseNumber contained comma-separated docket numbers in one entry. Companion dockets were inspected via fedcourts query --court scotus --docket-number.

The snapshot lists a separate October 13, 2026 federal respondents' opposition memorandum. The provisioned brief-in-opposition.txt contains the Authority's brief rather than that separate federal memorandum. A web open of its predecision docket link returned no usable content. The forecast uses the available private BIO and does not infer the federal memorandum's recommendation; prediction completed despite this limited gap.

The snapshot describes the filing only as a petition for certiorari. The official DOJ petition expressly seeks certiorari before judgment, a material vehicle distinction not visible in the staged docket text. Forecast incorporates that retrieved posture. Expected paper-only document absence is not a provisioning failure; no current-petition outcome was retrieved.

Snapshot's first entry reads 'Petition for a writ of certiorari filed', but the live supremecourt.gov docket reads 'Petition for a writ of certiorari before judgment filed'. The posture matters for the forecast; the snapshot text seems to have been normalized or captured before the Clerk amended it.

Frozen band is 'baseline' (cert_anchor 5.15%), but this petition is filed by the Solicitor General (D. John Sauer, counsel of record) on behalf of individual federal DEA task-force officers. The caption names only the officers, so the caption-class scorer reads it as private. In substance it belongs in the 'federal' class (pooled reached rate ~70%). Forecast departs from the frozen anchor accordingly.

Prediction-time statpack coverage cannot be reconstructed from staged result contents: claude-baseline, codex-baseline and gemini-baseline all report zero finer-resolved observations in their earlier pack, whereas the current committed OT2016–OT2025 pool has 1,337 finer-resolved and zero finer-unread observations. I preserved this apparent pack-vintage distinction, did not infer a candidate audit error from today's counts, and left baseline/skill values to the harness. This did not block evaluation.

gemini-baseline quotes the opening entry as an immediate administrative stay/stay pending appeal submitted to Justice Gorsuch and bases its standard/referral analysis on that description. The staged resolved docket instead says an injunction submitted to the Chief Justice; the application is addressed to Roberts and expressly distinguishes its affirmative All Writs Act injunction from a stay. This materially affects the rationale and forecast grades. The original candidate snapshot is not staged, so the origin of the historical-input versus prose mismatch cannot be established.

All three candidates describe application.txt as empty/non-OCR at prediction time. This evaluation receives 29,507 bytes of readable application text with empty_text=false and ocr_derived=true. The refreshed OCR was used to check the nature of the event, not imputed to candidates as information they had. No candidate is penalized merely for not analyzing the newly readable filing.

Historical baseline assertions cannot be fully reconciled from the staged evidence: claude-baseline reports zero finer-resolved counts/unread prior Terms, codex-baseline reports an older markdown table without finer counts, and gemini-baseline reports a populated finer pool. The current JSON pack has positive finer counts and zero finer_unread in 2016–2025, with several counts differing from gemini-baseline's table. Original statpack bytes/result bodies are not staged; pack evolution cannot be distinguished from misreading. No alternate baseline is supplied and the stamp remains authoritative.

claude-baseline (forward) web-fetched this application's own live supremecourt.gov docket at 2026-11-03T20:46Z, the same day the Chief Justice denied it. Only a result digest was captured. The candidate disclosed that no disposition appeared, and its timing forecast is consistent with that, so I graded the leakage not_applicable / not suspected. Noted because a forward cell run on the resolution date can see the outcome.

The candidates disagree about the statpack's interim finer counts. claude-baseline reported finer_resolved=0 and finer_unread non-zero. gemini-baseline reported populated finer counts that differ from the current statpack.json (e.g. OT2025 20/223 vs 19/218). The pack may have been rebuilt between prediction and evaluation. The harness-stamped interim baseline is unaffected, but maintainers may want the statpack digest pinned on interim predictions.

The provisioned paper-only arrival record contains no filed-document text or document manifest. I recovered the official DOJ petition, which clarifies that review is sought before judgment, but did not recover an opposition or independently read a separate lower-court opinion. Prediction completed using the snapshot, frozen federal anchor, and verified petition; the absence of opposition text remains an input limitation, not evidence that no opposition was filed.

Frozen band is 'baseline' (anchor 5.2%), but the petitioners are federal DEA task-force officers represented by the Solicitor General (D. John Sauer, counsel of record). In substance this is a federal-petitioner case, whose class floor is ~73% pooled. The caption rule reads 'Noah A. Herzon, et al.' as private. My forecast (0.80) follows the federal reality, not the band.

The staged argument transcript repeats 'ORAL ARGUMENT OF HELEN NORTON ON BEHALF OF THE RESPONDENTS' after Roberts introduces 'Rebuttal, Mr. Reaves?' and before Reaves's closing argument. argument-features.json consequently labels segment 3 respondent, with zero advocate turns and one other turn. Its 236/237 attributed Justice-turn coverage does not detect this header defect. I read the rebuttal as petitioners' from the actual speaker text and did not infer sentiment from aggregate counts or use the defective final segment. No inability to finish and no outcome material encountered.
